title: docs: keep existence checks out of the uniqueness resolvers and test explicit routes
body:
On `main`, an update of a missing link through `UniquenessResolver`, `CascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver` or `with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution()` returns `Ok` when the new pair is already stored, as the issue reports. The [follow-up comment](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/issues/66#issuecomment-6492359643) and the [Data.Doublets PR 527 review](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/527#issuecomment-6492081425) reject the suggested fix. A uniqueness resolver must not silently gain a compulsory existence check. Callers who want missing-address errors select that contract explicitly, and callers who guarantee valid operations can omit it. So this PR keeps the resolver unchanged, documents its contract, and tests the explicit routes.

- **Root cause.** Both resolvers look up the new `(source, target)` pair first. When it is stored, `resolve_address_change_conflict(old, new)` deletes `old` only `if old != new && links.exist(old)` (the C# `LinksUniquenessResolver.ResolveAddressChangeConflict` logic) and reports the survivor. A missing `old` never reaches the store's checked route. With a new pair, the update is forwarded and `CheckedMutation` returns `NotExists`, which explains the asymmetry.
- **Explicit error route.** Compose `.with_inner_reference_existence_validation()` *outside* the resolver, that is, after it in the builder chain. Both repro updates then return `Error::NotExists(99)` with no write and no callback. Inside the resolver, the validator is never reached for an existing pair, and a test pins this.
- **Per-call route.** `store.try_get_link(index)?` before the updates that need it.
- **Documentation.** A "Requested address" section and a doctest on `UniquenessResolver` and `CascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver`, a note on `with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution()`, a new table row and section in the doc-tested [mutation guide](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/issue-66-59e601628147/docs/mutation.md#updates-through-the-uniqueness-resolvers), a README note, and a patch changelog fragment.

The research checklist and decision record are in [`experiments/issue-66`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/tree/issue-66-59e601628147/experiments/issue-66).

## Reproduction

```rust
let mut s = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?
    .with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution();
s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?; s.create_link(1, 2)?;
s.update(99, 3, 3); // Err(NotExists(99))
s.update(99, 1, 2); // Ok(3), nothing changes: the resolver does not check 99
```

## Tests

`doublets/tests/uniqueness_missing_update.rs` runs each case on the unit and split layouts:

- `bare_store_rejects_missing_address` is the baseline.
- `validation_outside_{automatic_resolution,cascade_resolver,resolver}_rejects_missing_address`: both `update(99, 3, 3)` and `update(99, 1, 2)` return `NotExists(99)` with zero callbacks, and the count and links are unchanged.
- `{automatic_resolution,cascade_resolver,plain_resolver}_adds_no_existence_check` reproduces the report and pins that omitting the policy omits its work: the store is unchanged, and the single event is the stored `(3: 1 2)` link.
- `validation_inside_resolver_is_not_reached` shows that placement matters.
- `per_call_lookup_rejects_missing_address` covers the `try_get_link` route and checks that a live address still merges through the resolver.
- The resolver doctest and the mutation guide doctest run the composed stack.

## Validation

Run `bash experiments/issue-66/verify.sh`. It uses one Cargo job and writes its logs to `target/issue-66-logs/`.

[CI run 41541417592](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/actions/runs/41541417592) passed for commit `16c2d4f`: Linux, macOS and Windows tests, doc tests, lint and format, coverage, changelog and version guards, and the package build. CodeFactor also passed. Nothing was removed; the diff only adds lines. `main` has no new commits since this branch was created.

Local results:
- The new test file passes: 17 tests.
- `tests/decorators.rs` passes: 20 tests.
- The guide and resolver doctests pass.
- `cargo clippy -p doublets --tests --examples -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo doc` with `-Dwarnings` pass.
- The test-layout guard passes.

Fixes #66

title: feat: separate checked mutation from an explicitly unchecked store API
body:
Both memory stores built a compulsory `try_get_link(index)?` into `update_links` and `delete_links`. Omitting `InnerReferenceExistenceValidator` therefore did not omit that check, and the public API had no update primitive that a caller who already guarantees a live address could use. This PR keeps the minimal mutation mechanism in the store, puts the checks in explicit layers, and keeps the error and ignore-missing policies separate.

- **Minimal primitive.** `mem::UncheckedMutation::update_unchecked(index, source, target, handler)` is an `unsafe fn` on both layouts. It has two documented preconditions: `index` is live (not null, a service constant, beyond the allocated range, a free slot or released), and the indexes are consistent, as the store API maintains them. The endpoints are unconstrained. It detaches the old outgoing memberships, writes the endpoints, attaches the new ones and reports one event. Deletion is the caller's composition of an optional reset `update_unchecked(index, 0, 0)` and the existing `Release::release_unchecked`. Reset is a policy, so there is no third primitive.
- **Checked convenience in an explicit adapter.** `decorators::CheckedMutation` borrows the store, like `CheckedRelease`. It verifies only that the requested address is live and returns `Error::NotExists` before any write or callback. The stores' safe `update_links`/`delete_links` are now one-line delegations to it, so safe Rust APIs keep their behavior and stay memory-safe. A checked delete now does **one** lookup instead of four. A safe update with a short query or change slice reads missing parts as null instead of panicking on indexing.
- **Distinct policies.** `decorators::NonExistentDeletionResolver` (`with_non_existent_deletion_resolution()`, a port of C# `LinksNonExistentDeletionResolver`) is the ignore-missing policy. A missing requested address returns `Ok(Flow::Continue)` with no callback. A live address is forwarded unchanged, so `HasUsages`, `NonNullContents`, I/O and capacity errors still propagate. It does not validate endpoints or any other contract. The error policy remains the checked route and `InnerReferenceExistenceValidator`, and `NoExceptionsDecorator` remains the explicit swallow-all choice.
- **Documented route to omit checks.** The [mutation guide](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/issue-80-c1ec4fba6587/docs/mutation.md) gives the preconditions, a table of routes, and recipes for the checked, error, ignore, swallow and unchecked routes. It and the deletion guide are now compiled and run as doctests. The README, the [deletion guide](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/issue-80-c1ec4fba6587/docs/deletion.md), an executable `unchecked_mutation` example for both layouts, and a minor changelog fragment are included.

I rejected an `unsafe` constructor for a view that implements the safe `Links` trait without checks: safe code could then reach undefined behavior through it. The design rationale and the requirement-to-evidence map are in [`experiments/issue-80`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/tree/issue-80-c1ec4fba6587/experiments/issue-80).

## Reproduction

On `main`, `unit/store.rs` and `split/store.rs` call `try_get_link(index)?` in `update_links`. `delete_links` goes through `delete_with_reset`, which looks the link up four times: once itself, then in the reset resolver, the reset update and `CheckedRelease`. No caller could avoid these lookups. The new test-only `link_lookups` counter, which adds no production fields, measures them in the real stores.

## Tests

The tests never pass invalid addresses to unchecked APIs. Invalid addresses go only through the safe routes.

- **Safe rejection without mutation:** `safe_mutation_rejects_missing_addresses` (unit + split). It tries null, a released free-list slot, an address beyond the allocated range, `any` and `u32::MAX` on `update*`/`delete*` and on `CheckedMutation`. Each call returns `NotExists(index)` with zero callbacks, and the count, all links and the free list are unchanged (the released slot is reused next). Short slices give `NotExists(0)`.
- **Valid unchecked calls:** `valid_unchecked_updates` covers events, `Break` without undo, search and source indexes, self references, unallocated (external) endpoints, null endpoints, untouched neighbours, and composed reset+release followed by reuse. `checked_mutation_routes` covers the adapter's events and its single deletion event.
- **Omitting validation omits its work:** `unchecked_mutation_omits_validation_work` in `tests/internal/{unit,split}.rs` checks these counts:
  - checked update: 1 lookup and 1 primitive update;
  - rejected update/delete: 1 lookup each and 0 updates;
  - `update_unchecked`: **0** lookups and 1 update;
  - checked delete: 1 lookup;
  - unchecked reset + release: **0** lookups.
- **Policies are distinct:** `missing_deletion_is_ignored_only_when_selected` shows that the resolver ignores only missing deletions, still rejects updates, and forwards live deletions with their events; without the resolver, or with the validator, the result is `NotExists`. `missing_deletion_resolver_propagates_unrelated_errors` shows that `HasUsages` and `NonNullContents` still propagate, in contrast to `NoExceptionsDecorator`.
- The trait, adapter and resolver doctests and five guide doctests run on CI.

## Validation

Run `bash experiments/issue-80/verify.sh`. It uses one Cargo job and writes its logs to `target/issue-80-logs/`.

[CI run 41353284700](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/actions/runs/41353284700) passed for commit `4f296790b5b004166f20e0fe26b03ad52df38133`: Linux, macOS and Windows tests (the new tests and guide doctests are in the logs), lint, file size, coverage, changelog and version guards, and the package build. CodeFactor also passed.

Local results:
- `cargo test -p doublets`: all 35 test groups pass, including 10 new integration tests and 2 internal tests.
- The new tests also pass with `--no-default-features`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` with `-Dwarnings` passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo doc` with `-Dwarnings` pass.
- The test-layout guard passes, and every file is under the 1000-line limit.
- The example runs on both layouts.

One unrelated observation: if a link is given the same endpoints as another live link, which is a duplicate when uniqueness is not enforced, a later update can corrupt the size-balanced trees. The detach and attach logic is unchanged from `main`, so this PR does not introduce it. The new tests use distinct endpoints, as the uniqueness decorators guarantee.

`main` has no new commits since this branch was created.

Fixes #80

feat: separate link release from endpoint reset policy
body:
Deleting an already reset live link previously performed another backend `update(index, 0, 0)` in both memory layouts. This PR separates slot release from endpoint reset while preserving safe deletion helpers, incoming references, indexes, reuse, and callbacks.

- `mem::Release::release_unchecked` provides the minimal primitive with explicit live-address, detached-endpoint, and incoming-index preconditions. It performs required index/free-list/tail bookkeeping and the deletion callback.
- `release` / `release_with` check address and content conditions without transforming endpoints. Invalid addresses return `NotExists`; nonzero contents return `NonNullContents` without mutation or callbacks.
- `decorators::CheckedRelease` supplies release-only deletion for decorator stacks. Adding `NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver` explicitly enables automatic resetting. Already reset links skip the update.
- Existing `delete*` operations compose that resolver with checked release, preserving the original-state single deletion callback, former-index result, and callback control.
- Split-store incoming-index reclassification remains structural bookkeeping and reverses on address reuse. Usage rejection and cascades remain configurable policies.

The [deletion guide](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/issue-81-c1387393dd57/docs/deletion.md) documents contracts and all five supported routes; an executable example covers both layouts. A minor changelog fragment prepares the automated release.

## Review feedback: tests outside source directories

Moved all Rust source-tree test implementations into `tests/`, preserving all 12 library tests and seven FFI tests. The two release-script tests also moved into `scripts/tests/version_and_commit.rs`. Private-state suites are flat files under `doublets/tests/internal/`, included in their original module scope for private access. FFI tests now use the public bindings from `doublets-ffi/tests/ffi.rs`, supported by an additional `rlib` artifact alongside the C library outputs. Contributor guidance and verification references follow the new layout.

`check-test-layout.sh` failed on the four original source test files and the release script, and now confirms every Rust test implementation lives under `tests/`. CI runs the same check, plus regression fixtures with no ripgrep on PATH. The guard uses Git grep, and embedded script discovery uses standard grep, fixing the missing-tool failure found in the first fresh CI run. Package discovery also uses Git and standard grep, rejects a zero-package result, and has a mock-Cargo regression test to prevent silently skipped checks. [Preserved reproduction evidence and requirement mapping](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/tree/issue-81-c1387393dd57/experiments/issue-81) cover both the original bug and the review request.

## Reproduction and validation

Before the release fix, `deletion_of_reset_link_does_not_update_again` failed on both layouts: **3 backend updates observed versus 2 expected**. The relocated tests still verify actual backend update counts, including zero direct-release updates and exactly one resolver reset when needed. Release tests also cover self references, incoming source/target/overlapping usages, searches/counts, free-list/tail reuse, callbacks/results, callback breaks, and policy composition. Unchecked calls use valid reset live links.

Run `bash experiments/issue-81/verify.sh` for the full local checks with one Cargo job and reduced debug information.

title: refactor(decorators): consolidate in the main doublets library
body:
The separate decorator package contained only six aliases for implementations already in `doublets::decorators`. This PR removes its directory, workspace exclusion, standalone CI step, and developer commands. Decorators are maintained and tested through the main library, with no decorator implementation or public main-library API removed.

The README documents every former alias and how to retain the old transitive `full` feature selection. Stable Rust guidance, repository layout, and reusable verification scripts now describe the five maintained packages. Historical compiler logs and dependency snapshots remain clearly identified as historical evidence.

## Feature parity and regression coverage

`doublets/tests/decorator_consolidation.rs` preserves and expands the former compatibility test into 12 direct-constructor tests, covering all six exported decorators on both unit and split stores. They check uniqueness, validation errors, usage redirection, cascading composition, reset/deletion callbacks, and access to the wrapped store. The suite passes with default features, all features, and no default features.

That broader coverage exposed a pre-existing split-store bug: `create_link(point, 0)` produced a live link that `is_unused` classified as deleted because its target-tree size was zero. This broke usage validation and cascading deletion. Free-slot detection now checks both endpoint indexes. Two additional bare-store regressions cover the minimal case and free-list reuse/tail deletion with null endpoints.

The initial failures, complete export mapping, and requirement-to-evidence inventory are in [experiments/issue-83](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/tree/issue-83-0cc572283fd9/experiments/issue-83). The 14 new tests passed before the redundant package was removed and again after removal. No requested decorator functionality is deferred.

title: Allow source/target indexing to be selected independently from minimal link storage
body:
Architecture follow-up from [Data.Doublets PR #527](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/527#issuecomment-6492081425), corresponding to existing C# design issues [Data.Doublets #239](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/issues/239) and [#395](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/issues/395). No equivalent open/closed Rust issue was found in the audit.

At main `31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b`:

- [`unit::Store`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b/doublets/src/mem/unit/store.rs#L29) owns source and target tree implementations; its update path always maintains them.
- [`split::Store`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b/doublets/src/mem/split/store.rs#L31) owns four internal/external trees and always maintains the selected indexes.
- `unit::Store::is_unused` (lines 209–221) even uses source-tree size to distinguish freed slots, so simply substituting a no-op tree does not supply an independent index-free store.

Generic tree parameters allow implementing a tree strategy, but do not expose a documented minimal storage route that omits source/target indexing altogether. This couples an optional performance strategy to storage/liveness representation, contrary to the requested fully configurable layering.

Please design this separately: distinguish necessary slot allocation/liveness mechanisms from optional query indexes; allow an explicit index-free/minimal store or selected index layers; document query capabilities and costs for each choice. Preserve correct bookkeeping for existing indexed stores, including split internal/external reclassification, instead of disabling maintenance of an index that remains selected.

Verification should cover creation/update/delete/reuse and liveness without tree metadata, then equivalent indexed behavior when the index layers are present, with measured overhead and no per-call unused-policy branch. This is an architectural enhancement, not a claim that current indexed operation under its documented preconditions is corrupt. PR #527 records the finding; implementation belongs in a separate change.

title: Make deletion endpoint reset an explicit layer over a minimal release primitive
body:
Separate architecture follow-up from [Data.Doublets PR #527's review](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/527#issuecomment-6492081425).

At main `31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b`, both root stores unconditionally reset contents during deletion:

- [unit `delete_links`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b/doublets/src/mem/unit/store.rs#L547), line 555: `self.update(index, T::from_byte(0), T::from_byte(0))?`.
- [split `delete_links`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b/doublets/src/mem/split/store.rs#L862), line 872: the same unconditional update.

Rust already exposes `NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver` and `.with_non_null_contents_deletion_resolution()`, but leaving that layer out does not omit endpoint reset. Even callers that have already detached a link must go through an additional update. In C# the raw release operation requires reset endpoints, and the resolver explicitly supplies that transformation.

Please introduce/document a minimal release primitive with explicit live-address, detached-endpoint and incoming-usage preconditions, then put optional automatic resetting in the resolver or a checked/convenience adapter. Preserve safe Rust's safety guarantees and valid deletion callbacks/results. The necessary detachment/reclassification of entries in the chosen index representation is structural bookkeeping and must remain correct; this is not a request to remove it.

Verification should distinguish direct release of an already reset live link from deletion through the resetting layer, show no redundant reset/update on the minimal route, and retain coverage for self references, incoming usages, both layouts, reuse and callbacks. Do not call invalid unchecked memory in tests.

Searched all open/closed issues: #58 ports the resolver, and #67 fixes callback visibility in a cascade; neither separates unconditional backend reset from the optional reset policy. Data.Doublets PR #527 documents this current Rust gap and leaves this implementation to a separate change as requested.

title: Separate compulsory mutation contract checks from an explicitly unchecked store API
body:
Found during the architecture review requested in [Data.Doublets PR #527](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/pull/527#issuecomment-6492081425). This is a separate follow-up, not a request to change safe Rust methods into unsound unchecked methods.

At main `31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b`, both memory backends embed existence validation in `update_links` and `delete_links`:

- [unit store](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b/doublets/src/mem/unit/store.rs#L494): `try_get_link(index)?` at lines 504 and 554.
- [split store](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/31b38458efbd277b399e46b22474b85a85bda24b/doublets/src/mem/split/store.rs#L786): `try_get_link(index)?` at lines 796 and 868.

`InnerReferenceExistenceValidator` is already optional, but omitting it does not omit the backend check. The public store surface has no unchecked update/delete primitive. Callers that already guarantee live addresses cannot select a mutation path without redundant contract verification.

A bounded probe of both raw and automatically decorated united/split stores confirms the current behavior: 48 store/scenario/API combinations and 96 missing deletions all return `Error::NotExists`, with no callbacks or state changes. These results show that C# issue #518's corruption does not reproduce; they do not demonstrate configurable contract validation. The reusable probe is `experiments/missing_delete.rs` in Data.Doublets PR #527.

Requested separate change:

1. Specify the minimal storage mutation preconditions and expose an appropriate explicitly `unsafe` primitive (or equivalent statically selected unchecked implementation) for callers that guarantee them.
2. Keep safe Rust APIs memory-safe. Implement checked convenience behavior and typed missing-link errors in explicit adapters/validators, with a documented route to omit those checks when the caller takes responsibility.
3. Keep throw/error and ignore-missing policies distinct. Do not swallow unrelated errors or make a resolver implicitly validate unrelated contracts.
4. Test safe rejection without mutation, valid unchecked calls, and that omitting validation omits its work. Never test invalid unchecked addresses in-process.

Searched all open and closed issues before reporting: #58 supplies optional decorators, and #66 concerns uniqueness-resolver behavior, but neither tracks the compulsory backend validation/bypass gap. The C# PR documents current Rust limitations; implementation belongs here separately.

title: fix: return documented indexes from deletion helpers
body:
Fixes #64.

`delete(3)` and `delete_by([3])` returned zero because they selected the empty post-deletion link's index. `rebase_and_delete(2, 1)` forwarded that deletion result instead of returning the replacement address.

The shared trait now reads `before.index` for deletion and maps successful deletion to `new` for rebasing. Both storage backends and the automatic decorator stack inherit the fix. Missing-address errors, the self-rebase shortcut, and callback behavior are preserved. A `bump: patch` changelog fragment prepares the automatic release. The README and lockfile are synchronized with the v0.12.0 release merged from `main`.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

```rust
let mut store = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?;
store.create_point()?;
store.create_point()?;
store.create_point()?;
assert_eq!(store.delete(3)?, 3);
assert_eq!(store.rebase_and_delete(2, 1)?, 1);
```

```sh
cargo test -p doublets --test deletion_returns --all-features -- --test-threads=1
```

The new suite reproduced 22 failures returning zero before the implementation change; the four error/self-rebase cases already passed. All 26 tests pass after the fix. Coverage includes direct and query deletion, uninitialized links, allocated-address holes, rebasing with and without usages, cascaded deletion, missing addresses, and self-rebasing on unit/split stores, bare and automatically decorated. title: fix: preserve split-store references to IDs created later
body:
Fixes #74.

`split::Store` now keeps a reference searchable when the referenced ID is created later. The issue's query returns `[2]`, matching the united store and the C# implementation. References to IDs that do not exist remain valid.

### The example, step by step

A link has an ID and two numbers called its **source** and **target**. Think of it as a card with a number on top and two numbers written on it. `(2: 3 2)` means card 2 has source 3 and target 2. Writing 3 on card 2 does not require card 3 to exist yet.

The issue does this:

1. Create links 1 and 2, initially pointing to themselves.
2. Change link 2 to `(2: 3 2)`. Link 3 does not exist yet.
3. Create link 3 as `(3: 3 3)`.
4. Ask for links whose source is 3 and target is 2: `[any, 3, 2]`. Here `any` means the link's own ID can be anything.

The answer should be `[2]`: creating link 3 did not change what was written on link 2.

| Read operation | Before the fix | After the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read link 2 directly with `get_link(2)` | `Some(2: 3 2)` | `Some(2: 3 2)` |
| United store: query `[any, 3, 2]` after creating 3 | `[2]` | `[2]` |
| Split store: the same query before creating 3 | `[2]` | `[2]` |
| Split store: the same query after creating 3 | `[]` | `[2]` |

### Why united and split behaved differently

An **index** is a lookup table: it lets the store find cards by their source or target without reading every card. Reading by ID goes straight to the card. That is why `get_link(2)` could still work while a query failed.

The **united store**, exposed in Rust as `unit::Store`, keeps link data and index metadata together in one memory region. It has two store-wide trees, one for sources and one for targets. These trees index the written numbers whether or not the referenced links exist. Creating link 3 does not change where the source entry for `(2: 3 2)` is found.

The **split store**, `split::Store`, keeps data and index metadata in separate memory regions. Inside Rust's split store, references to missing IDs use the store-wide **external indexes**. References to live IDs use **internal indexes** rooted at those IDs. In the example, link 2's source entry starts in the external source tree because link 3 is absent. Once link 3 is created, source queries for 3 use its internal index.

The old creation code already tried to move those entries. However, it marked ID 3 as live **before** asking the ordinary query path to find references to 3. That query immediately switched to the new, empty internal index. It found no entries to move, leaving link 2's source entry in the external index. Later queries looked in the internal index and missed it.

### What changes

The existing resolver now asks the external source tree directly for references to the new ID. It collects their link IDs, then moves each entry using the existing detach/attach operations. It repeats that for the external target tree. Collecting first avoids editing a tree while walking through it. Both passes finish before the creation callback runs.

The two passes matter: a link can use the new ID in both endpoints and needs an entry in both indexes. The same repair handles creating a new ID and reusing a deleted ID. Subsequent updates and deletions can then remove entries from the same indexes that queries use.

The regression tests also exposed an incorrect count: an exact pair with a missing source counted every link using that source, even those with a different target. Source-only counting now applies only when the target is `any`; exact counts check both numbers. The test fixture previously counted `4` instead of `1`.

All of this happens **within one split store**. Link IDs, stored source/target values, the API, and the memory layout stay the same. Conversion between united and split stores is outside this issue's scope. The fix keeps the existing resolver with two explicit passes and a corrected wildcard condition. Optional tracing is disabled by default; `DOUBLETS_TRACE_SPLIT_INDEXES=1` logs which index entries were moved.

### Comparison with C#

I checked and ran the C# sources at [`Data.Doublets` revision `f8c521e`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/tree/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693), the current main when reviewed. Its united and split stores both return `[2]` before and after creating ID 3, for source and target variants of the example.

C#'s split store chooses indexes using the configured `ExternalReferencesRange`, rather than whether a link currently exists. A small internal ID such as 3 uses its internal index even before link 3 exists, provided its slot is in reserved memory. Creating link 3 does not change that choice. See C#'s [`Update`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693/csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets/Memory/Split/Generic/SplitMemoryLinksBase.cs#L613), [`Each`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693/csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets/Memory/Split/Generic/SplitMemoryLinksBase.cs#L434), and [`Create`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693/csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets/Memory/Split/Generic/SplitMemoryLinksBase.cs#L694). Its [`Count`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693/csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets/Memory/Split/Generic/SplitMemoryLinksBase.cs#L298) also checks both endpoints for an exact pair.

The Rust repair matches these observable results while retaining Rust's existing index design. It avoids a wider redesign or a new rule rejecting missing-ID references. The comparison covers 12 cases: united, split with its default source linked list, split with a source tree, source/target references, and external-reference support on/off. Each case verifies exact/wildcard enumeration and counts against a full scan, multiple usages, an absent pair, and unchanged endpoints. All 12 pass. This verifies the issue's small example, rather than claiming complete C#/Rust equivalence or C# support for IDs beyond reserved memory.

The [comparison notes](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/issue-74-b2cc25ca247c/experiments/issue-74/csharp-comparison.md) include pinned source links, the probe, and results. No changes in another repository are needed for this reproduction.

### Reproduce and verify

```sh
cargo run -p doublets --example forward_references
cargo test -p doublets --test split_forward_reference --all-features
bash experiments/issue-74/verify.sh
# Optional C# comparison; requires gh and a .NET SDK:
bash experiments/issue-74/compare-csharp.sh
```

Before the original fix, seven of eight initial regressions failed while the united-store control passed. All nine final regressions pass: both endpoint directions, exact and wildcard reads/counts/search, multiple usages, two missing endpoints created separately, later updates/deletions, tail recreation, free-list reuse, and `Flow::Break` callbacks. The plain-map differential check runs four fixed seeds of 256 operations per backend, with at most 24 live links and references in `1..=32`.

The patch changelog fragment prepares the next release through the existing release workflow. The README dependency and lockfile are synchronized with the manifest's existing 0.8.0 version.

Local validation passed on Rust 1.99.0 with one build job and reduced debug information: all 326 workspace tests, separate default-feature doctests (four passed), strict Clippy across workspace targets/features, formatting, release and documentation builds, package listing, the example, and file-size/badge/toolchain/changelog/version checks. One pre-existing doctest is ignored. Logs are under `target/issue-74-logs/`. The optional C# probe passed all 12 cases with SDK 10.0.112 and runtime roll-forward to .NET 10. Current main (`02b3c9b`) is already included.

On final commit `1dba31bf85a9d9cc4e709afdeed97fd4c81676fe`, [CI run 40667048640](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/actions/runs/40667048640) passed tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and [CodeFactor](https://www.codefactor.io/repository/github/linksplatform/doublets-rs/pull/75) reports no issues. The [full pipeline for the Rust changes](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/actions/runs/40666511125) also passed lint, coverage, changelog, and package checks; change detection skips those jobs for the final C#-probe-only refactor. The complete PR diff has been reviewed, current main is included, and the working tree is clean.

title: split::Store loses a link that refers to an id created later
body:
## Summary

`split::Store` of doublets 0.8.0 loses a link from its indexes when the link
refers to an id whose link is created only later. Once that link exists, a
concrete query for the pair finds nothing, although `get_link` still returns
the link. `unit::Store` finds it.

## Minimal reproduction (doublets 0.8.0, Rust 1.99.1, Linux x86_64)

`Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "split-forward-reference"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[dependencies]
doublets = "0.8.0"
```

`src/main.rs`:

```rust
use doublets::{Doublets, data::Flow, mem::Global, split, unit};

fn run<D: Doublets<usize>>(name: &str, mut links: D) {
    let _a = links.create_point().unwrap(); // 1 = (1, 1)
    let b = links.create_point().unwrap(); // 2 = (2, 2)
    links.update(b, 3, b).unwrap(); // 2 = (3, 2): link 3 does not exist yet
    let c = links.create_point().unwrap(); // 3 = (3, 3)
    let any = links.constants().any;
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    links.each_by([any, c, b], |link| {
        found.push(link.index);
        Flow::Continue
    });
    println!("{name}: each_by([any, 3, 2]) -> {found:?}, get_link(2) -> {:?}", links.get_link(b));
}

fn main() {
    run("united", unit::Store::<usize, _>::new(Global::new()).unwrap());
    run("split", split::Store::<usize, _, _>::new(Global::new(), Global::new()).unwrap());
}
```

Output:

```
united: each_by([any, 3, 2]) -> [2], get_link(2) -> Some(2: 3 2)
split: each_by([any, 3, 2]) -> [], get_link(2) -> Some(2: 3 2)
```

Expected: `split` returns `[2]`, as `united` does.

## Notes

- doublets 0.5.0 also lost links whose references all existed (for example
  after `update 3 = (4, 3)`); 0.8.0 fixes that case, and only the reference to a
  not yet created id remains. The differential check, its log for both
  versions and the commands are in
  [Comparisons.RedisVSDoublets/experiments/rust-split-internal-references](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.RedisVSDoublets/tree/issue-13-f67d791f1225/experiments/rust-split-internal-references).
- A likely cause is that the split store chooses the index tree (internal or
  external) of a source or target from whether that id exists when the link is
  written, and does not move the link when the id is created. If such
  references are not supported, `update`/`create` could return an error
  instead of keeping a link that queries cannot find.

## Workaround downstream

`Comparisons.RedisVSDoublets` runs the random changes of its split-store test
with references to existing links only, and does not delete a link that
others refer to (`rust/tests/same_behavior.rs`, `References::Existing`).

title: fix: deduplicate overlapping usages and deletion matches
body:
Fixes #63.

A link that references a value through both endpoints was counted and listed twice. Deleting those usages, or deleting the matches of `[any, value]`, then tried to delete the same index twice and returned `NotExists` after successfully deleting it.

Usage helpers now treat each other referencing link as one usage. `count_usages` subtracts the source/target overlap before excluding the referenced link itself. `usages` and `delete_usages_with` skip overlapping matches in the target pass, following the existing decorator helper. `delete_query_with` deduplicates indices while collecting matches and preserves reverse order of first occurrence. Deletion handlers retain their existing fused behavior after `Flow::Break`.

The patch release is prepared through `changelog.d/20261008_233000_issue_63_distinct_usages.md`. The branch includes main's 0.7.0 release and the transaction and rebase fixes from PRs #71 and #72. The README dependency snippet and lockfile are synchronized with the released manifest version.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

On `(1: 1 1) (2: 2 2) (3: 1 2) (4: 3 3)`:

| Operation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count_usages(3)` | `Ok(2)` | `Ok(1)` |
| `usages(3)` | `Ok([4, 4])` | `Ok([4])` |
| `delete_usages(3)` | Deletes 4, then `Err(NotExists(4))` | Deletes 4 once and returns `Ok(())` |

On the first three links, `delete_query_with([any, 1], ..)` returned `Err(NotExists(1))` after deleting its matches. It now deletes links 1 and 3 once each and returns `Ok(())`.

body:
Fixes #62.

title: feat(transactions): add generic transactions and durable recovery
body:
Consumers previously had to build their own transaction layer. This adds a generic `TransactionsDecorator` with an exclusively borrowed handle: commit preserves its writes, explicit rollback restores the original graph, and dropping an unfinished handle rolls back, including during unwinding.

Fixes #61.

### Changes

- Add `Transition` before/after records with create/update/delete kinds, ordered transaction/sequence IDs, and idempotent apply/revert on raw stores.
- Add `MemoryTransitionLog` and a versioned `FileTransitionLog`. File appends synchronize checksummed records; reopening discards a torn final record and rejects complete corruption or addresses that cannot fit the requested reference type.
- Persist a complete before snapshot at begin and after snapshot at commit. Store callbacks run after mutation and the store interface has no flush hook, so these snapshots close the callback gap and support undo/redo without assuming backend writes persisted.
- Add `DecoratorsExt::with_transactions`, policy composition around the handle, optional tracing, and exposed drop-time rollback errors. Journal errors block further writes until recovery.
- Fix split-store self-reference classification before index detachment. The minimal regression previously returned zero internal target matches instead of one, then panicked during a later reset; both operations now succeed.
- Use collection assertions compatible with Rust 1.99's Clippy lint in the new recovery tests.
- Add usage documentation, a runnable example, reusable investigation/verification scripts, and a minor-release changelog fragment. Correct the README install version to match the existing manifest.

```rust
let mut store = raw.with_transactions(MemoryTransitionLog::default())?;
let mut tx = store.begin_transaction()?;
let point = tx.create_point()?;
tx.commit()?;
```

Snapshots use space proportional to the graph and the journal has no automatic retention. Recovery requires an exclusively owned, matching journal and structurally readable raw store; it cannot repair torn backend tree indexes. Nested transactions are rejected. A commit I/O failure has an indeterminate durable outcome until recovery. These limits and decorator ordering are documented.

### Reproduction and validation

The initial transaction regression could not compile on the previous code because the public transaction API was absent. `dropping_an_uncommitted_transaction_restores_the_graph` now verifies that update/delete/create are undone with original addresses preserved. `split_self_reference.rs` reproduced the separate indexing bug before its fix.

23 new tests cover both backends, commit/rollback/drop, address reuse and holes, policy writes, handler unwinding, failed writes, injected journal/restoration failures, reversible transitions, corrupt/torn journals, address narrowing, and recovery after subprocess exit without destructors. Recovery tests also cover a mutation with no callback record and a committed graph with no backend writes persisted.

Local validation passed on Rust 1.99 with CI's `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings`: formatting, strict Clippy, all workspace/all-feature tests, documentation tests, release build, documentation build, package file listing, the transactions example, and repository size/badge/toolchain/release-fragment checks. Reproduce with `bash experiments/issue-61/verify.sh`; logs are written per check.

title: feat(sequences): add C# compatible Unicode string pipeline
body:
Fixes #60.

Rust consumers can now build the store-backed sequence and Unicode string pipeline from `Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences` 0.6.5 using `doublets::sequences`, without carrying an application-local port.

## Implementation

Adds every counterpart listed in the issue:

- `BalancedVariantConverter`, `AddressToRawNumberConverter`, `RawNumberToAddressConverter` and `CachingConverterDecorator` in `sequences::converters`.
- `CharToUnicodeSymbolConverter`, `UnicodeSymbolToCharConverter`, `StringToUnicodeSequenceConverter` and `UnicodeSequenceToStringConverter` in `sequences::unicode`.
- `RightSequenceWalker` in `sequences::walkers`, with lazy iteration and collected traversal.
- `DefaultStack` and `TargetMatcher`, also available directly from `sequences`. The reusable `TargetMatcher` and `CriterionMatcher` are exposed through `doublets::data` and the crate root.

Converters accept a store per operation, share the existing `Doublets` interface, reuse pairs through `get_or_create`, and work with either backend. Marker addresses belong to the caller. The module is always available and adds no dependencies.

Encoding follows C#: adjacent pairs are combined layer by layer, odd tails carry forward, symbols store `(raw UTF-16 unit, symbol marker)`, nonempty strings store `(balanced root, sequence marker)`, and the sequence marker itself denotes an empty string. Stores must enable external references. Character conversion uses `u16`; `convert_utf16` preserves lone surrogates, while conversion to a Rust `String` reports invalid UTF-16.

The raw-number converters implement C# hybrid encoding directly: external zero is `MAX / 2 + 1`, and positive magnitudes are encoded as unsigned negatives. The existing `platform-data` 2.0.0 `Hybrid` helper has incompatible zero/absolute-value behavior, so using it would corrupt this encoding. Its existing public behavior is unchanged.

Typed errors report invalid ranges, missing links, wrong markers and cycles. The walker uses a heap stack and tracks the active path so repeated subtrees retain every occurrence. Successful conversions can be cached; callers clear caches after changing underlying links. Writes follow the existing store API and are not transactional.

## Reproduction and compatibility

`doublets/tests/sequences.rs` initially failed with `unresolved import doublets::sequences`. Its minimal pipeline regression encodes `"A\0😀"`, asserts all eight resulting link triples, decodes the text, and checks repeated encoding and empty strings.

The same pipeline was run against the actual C# NuGet package, version 0.6.5. All eight triples match exactly, including external zero and the emoji's surrogate pair. The independently runnable comparison is preserved in `experiments/issue-60/verify-compatibility.sh`; it needs the .NET 10 SDK. It checks graph encoding rather than binary store-file layout.

Eleven automated tests cover both backends and multiple address widths, odd tails, shared subtrees, raw-number boundaries, invalid payloads, lone surrogates, missing links, cycles, cache retries/invalidation and store-error propagation. A bounded 2,048-link walk runs on a 128 KiB thread stack.

The module documentation and `doublets/examples/unicode_strings.rs` provide runnable encoding/decoding/caching examples. The README dependency snippet and lockfile are synchronized with the existing 0.5.0 manifest. The minor release is prepared through the changelog fragment, as the automated release workflow requires; package manifests are unchanged.

CI's Rust 1.99.0 introduced `clippy::assert_is_empty`, which rejected five existing test assertions in the [initial feature run](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/actions/runs/37857084681/job/113583968852). Reproducing with that toolchain also caught the new walker's empty-result assertion. All six now use equivalent typed empty-array comparisons. The investigation and saved log locations are documented in `experiments/issue-60/README.md`.

## Validation

Passed locally (strict Clippy, full workspace tests and repository checks also rerun on CI's Rust 1.99.0):

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: resize_mem returns only the grown region, causing unit-store panics after 1,040,383 links
body:
## Reproduction (released 0.5.0 and current main)

The `new_cap > current` branch in `doublets/src/mem/mod.rs::resize_mem`
returns `RawMem::grow_filled(...)`. `platform-mem` 0.3.0 returns only the added
region, whereas the unit store treats this slice as its complete allocation.
The initial growth from 8,192 to 2^20 records therefore exposes only 1,040,384
records while the header reserves 2^20 - 1.

A complete executable reproduction already exists in
[Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets/experiments/unit_store_growth](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets/tree/main/experiments/unit_store_growth).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets.git
cd Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets
cargo build --manifest-path experiments/unit_store_growth/Cargo.toml --locked --release
(ulimit -v 524288; RUST_BACKTRACE=full experiments/unit_store_growth/target/release/unit_store_growth bare)
(ulimit -v 524288; RUST_BACKTRACE=full experiments/unit_store_growth/target/release/unit_store_growth whole)
```

On Linux x86_64 / Rust 1.98.1, the finite probe has a 512 MiB virtual-memory
limit. `bare` panics creating link 1,040,384 with `Data part should be in data
memory` and returns `Err(Any { .. })`. The program intentionally catches the
panic, so its process exit code is zero; inspect its output. `whole` completes
2,097,153 links, including subsequent growth, and prints `Ok(Ok(2097153))`.
The unmodified call remains present on current main, so this is not solely
an obsolete-release problem. The earlier benchmark failure is recorded in
[run 37224809082](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets/actions/runs/37224809082).

## Workaround

Wrap the RawMem backend so grow/grow_filled return the whole allocation.
The comparison repository already does this in
[rust/src/memory.rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/Comparisons.SQLiteVSDoublets/blob/main/rust/src/memory.rs)
(`Whole<M>`), for both volatile and file-mapped backends.

## Suggested code fix

In `resize_mem`, perform `m.grow_filled(new_cap - current, M::Item::default())?;`
then return `Ok(m.allocated_mut())`, matching the shrink/no-change branches.
Check other growth call sites for the same slice-contract assumption. Add
tests asserting initial capacity and subsequent growth retain earlier links
for unit/split and global/file-mapped stores. Small mock RawMem backends can
exercise the contract without creating millions of links in unit tests.

title: with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution: cascaded deletions skip the reset to (0 0) that C# reports
body:
Found while working on https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/106, with `doublets` 0.5.0 (`main` is the same commit, 1d54fd6). Low priority: the final state is correct, only the reported changes differ.

## Repro

```rust
let mut s = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?
    .with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution();
s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?; s.create_link(1, 2)?; s.create_link(3, 3)?;
s.delete_with(1, |before, after| { println!("{before:?} -> {after:?}"); Flow::Continue })?;
```

## Actual

```text
(1: 1 1) -> (1: 0 0)
(4: 3 3) -> ()
(3: 1 2) -> ()
(1: 0 0) -> ()
```

## Expected (C# Platform.Data.Doublets 0.18.1, `DecorateWithAutomaticUniquenessAndUsagesResolution`)

```text
(1: 1 1) -> (1: 0 0)
(3: 1 2) -> (3: 0 0)
(4: 3 3) -> (4: 0 0)
(4: 0 0) -> ()
(3: 0 0) -> ()
(1: 0 0) -> ()
```

## Root cause

[`with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/builder.rs#L116-L128) puts `CascadeUsagesResolver` innermost, below `NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver`, as C# does. C# re-enters the cascade through `_facade`, so every nested deletion goes through the reset layer. The Rust [`cascade`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/usages.rs#L74-L93) deletes through `self.links`, below that layer, so the nested deletions skip the reset to `(0 0)`.

The crate's own docs advise against this stack:

- [`CascadeUsagesResolver`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/usages.rs#L64-L69): "place this decorator above the layers whose behaviour the cascade must observe";
- [`decorators` module docs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/mod.rs#L53-L55): "For a stack whose outermost layer is the one doing the recursion the two are the same, which is the case for every stack C# itself builds". Here the recursing layer is the innermost one.

The visited set that lets cycles terminate is a good deviation and should stay.

## Suggested fix

Either let `cascade` reset each usage to `(0 0)` before deleting it, or build this stack with the cascade above the reset layer. Then correct the module docs.

title: CascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver: update of a missing link returns Ok when the new pair already exists
body:
Found while working on https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/106, with `doublets` 0.5.0 (`main` is the same commit, 1d54fd6).

## Repro

```rust
let mut s = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?
    .with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution();
s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?; s.create_link(1, 2)?;   // (1: 1 1) (2: 2 2) (3: 1 2)
s.update(99, 3, 3);   // Err(NotExists(99)), as expected
s.update(99, 1, 2);   // Ok(3), nothing changes
```

## Expected

`Err(NotExists(99))` in both cases; the plain store returns it for both.

## Root cause

[`CascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver::update_links`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/uniqueness.rs#L133-L148) searches for the new pair first and, when it exists, goes to [`resolve_address_change_conflict`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/uniqueness.rs#L156-L172), which skips the deletion because `old` does not exist and reports the survivor. Nothing checks that `old` exists.

## Suggested fix

Call `self.links.try_get_link(old)?` before the search.

title: delete_all fails with NotExists, deleting nothing or only part of the store, when the store has holes
body:
Found while working on https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/106, with `doublets` 0.5.0 (`main` is the same commit, 1d54fd6).

## Repro

```rust
let mut s = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?;
s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?;
s.delete(2)?;          // store: (1: 1 1) (3: 3 3)
s.delete_all()?;       // Err(NotExists(2)), nothing deleted
```

With the hole at 1 instead (`(2: 2 2) (3: 3 3)`), `delete_all` returns `Err(NotExists(1))` and `(3: 3 3)` is left.

## Expected

An empty store.

## Root cause

[`delete_all`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L231-L242) deletes the address equal to `count()`, which is the highest address only when the store has no holes.

## Suggested fix

Collect the indices of `each_iter([any])` and delete them in reverse order.

title: delete, delete_by and rebase_and_delete return 0 instead of the documented index
body:
Found while working on https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/106, with `doublets` 0.5.0 (`main` is the same commit, 1d54fd6).

## Repro

```rust
let mut s = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?;
s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?; s.create_point()?;
assert_eq!(s.delete(3)?, 3);                // fails: returns 0
assert_eq!(s.rebase_and_delete(2, 1)?, 1);  // fails: returns 0
```

`delete` behaves the same with `with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution()`.

## Expected

[`delete`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L215-L221) is documented as "returns its former index", [`delete_by`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L193-L204) as "returns the deleted link's index", and [`rebase_and_delete`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L531-L543) as "Returns `new`".

## Root cause

`delete_by` keeps `after.index`, but after a deletion `after` is the empty link, so its index is always 0. `rebase_and_delete` returns `self.delete(old)`.

## Suggested fix

Keep `before.index` in `delete_by`, and end `rebase_and_delete` with `self.delete(old).map(|_| new)`.

title: usages and count_usages list a link twice when it uses the value as both source and target; delete_usages and delete_query_with then fail with NotExists
body:
Found while working on https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/106, with `doublets` 0.5.0 (`main` is the same commit, 1d54fd6).

## Repro

On `unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())` holding `(1: 1 1) (2: 2 2) (3: 1 2) (4: 3 3)`:

| Call | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `s.count_usages(3)` | `Ok(2)` | `Ok(1)` |
| `s.usages(3)` | `Ok([4, 4])` | `Ok([4])` |
| `s.delete_usages(3)` | deletes 4, then `Err(NotExists(4))` | `Ok(())` |

On `(1: 1 1) (2: 2 2) (3: 1 2)`, `s.delete_query_with([any, 1], ..)` deletes 3 and 1, then returns `Err(NotExists(1))`. The links are gone, but the caller sees an error.

## Root cause

A link that references a value as both its source and its target is found twice:

- [`delete_query_with`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L244-L264) collects `each_by(query)`, and `[any, v]` visits `(v: v v)` twice: once as a source usage, once as a target usage;
- [`delete_usages_with`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L266-L295) and [`usages`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L436-L458) append the `[any, v, any]` and `[any, any, v]` results;
- [`count_usages`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L414-L434) sums both counts.

The second deletion of the same index then fails with `NotExists`. C# [`DeleteAllUsages`](https://github.com/linksplatform/Data.Doublets/blob/f8c521e539935e670f4f484cf451857d2bd3e693/csharp/Platform.Data.Doublets/ILinksExtensions.cs#L1040-L1060) does not fail, because it skips usages that no longer exist.

## Suggested fix

In the second pass, skip the links whose source is the value, as [`helpers::usages_of`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/helpers.rs#L62-L76) already does. Or remove duplicate indices before deleting.

title: rebase_with leaves a link that uses old as both source and target pointing at old
body:
Found while working on https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/106, with `doublets` 0.5.0 (`main` is the same commit, 1d54fd6).

## Repro

```rust
use doublets::{mem::Global, unit, Doublets, Flow};

let mut s = unit::Store::<u32, _>::new(Global::new())?;
s.create_point()?;          // (1: 1 1)
s.create_point()?;          // (2: 2 2)
s.create_link(1, 2)?;       // (3: 1 2)
s.create_link(3, 3)?;       // (4: 3 3)
s.create_link(2, 1)?;       // (5: 2 1)
s.rebase_with(3, 5, |before, after| { println!("{before:?} -> {after:?}"); Flow::Continue })?;
```

## Actual

Four updates, and link 4 ends as `(4: 3 5)`; it still uses `3`:

```text
(4: 3 3) -> (4: 5 3)
(4: 5 3) -> (4: 3 5)
(4: 3 5) -> (4: 5 3)
(4: 5 3) -> (4: 3 5)
```

The same happens with `with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution()`.

## Expected

One update, `(4: 3 3) -> (4: 5 5)`.

## Root cause

[`rebase_with`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/data/traits.rs#L482-L520) collects the usages from `[any, old, any]` and from `[any, any, old]` without removing duplicates, so a link that uses `old` on both sides is processed twice. Each pass then builds the update from the stale copy taken before any update (`[usage.index, new, usage.target]`, then `[usage.index, usage.source, new]`), so every second update undoes the first one.

## Suggested fix

Remove duplicate usage indices (as [`helpers::usages_of`](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/blob/1d54fd692960258b9b72380e67e2c4f6369372bf/doublets/src/decorators/helpers.rs#L62-L76) already does) and issue one update per usage:
`[i, if s == old { new } else { s }, if t == old { new } else { t }]`.

Related: the C# counterpart `MergeUsages` has its own bug, linksplatform/Data.Doublets#515.

title: No transactions layer: C# has UInt64LinksTransactionsLayer, Rust has nothing
body:
## Summary

`doublets` has no transactions layer. C# has shipped one in `Platform.Data.Doublets` for years (`UInt64LinksTransactionsLayer`, `ITransaction`, `Transition`), so a consumer that wants "apply these writes or none of them" has to write the layer itself in Rust.

```console
$ grep -rli transaction doublets-0.5.0/src
$      # no matches
```

## What is missing

The pieces C# has and Rust does not:

- a transaction handle with `Commit`/`Rollback`, rolling back on drop when neither was called;
- a transition record — `(before, after)` doublets plus a kind — appended per write;
- a durable transition log, so an interrupted process can be recovered rather than left half-written;
- replay/revert of a transition, which is what both rollback and recovery are built from.

Every one of these is generic over the store, which is exactly the kind of thing [`decorators`](https://docs.rs/doublets/0.5.0/doublets/decorators/index.html) is already the home for: a `TransactionsDecorator` would compose the same way `UniquenessResolver` does.

## Evidence

[link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli) needed this in both languages and had to write the Rust half from scratch:

- [`rust/src/transactions/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/tree/3d53362125be47de595b0cad7a24fe4c3aeefd3d/rust/src/transactions) — ~1570 lines: the decorator, the transition types, and a file-backed transition log with retention policies

`WriteHandler` already gives a decorator the `(before, after)` pair a transition needs, so the store-facing half of the work is done — what is missing is the layer that collects them, makes them durable, and can play them backwards.

## Related, if this is taken on

Two layers built on top of the same transition stream, also written by hand in the same repo, would become straightforward for any consumer once transactions exist upstream:

- [`version_control/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/tree/3d53362125be47de595b0cad7a24fe4c3aeefd3d/rust/src/version_control) — branches, tags and checkout over the transition sequence (~670 lines)
- [`persistent_transformations.rs`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/3d53362125be47de595b0cad7a24fe4c3aeefd3d/rust/src/persistent_transformations.rs) — triggers re-applied after every write (~670 lines)

title: No Rust counterpart for Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences (sequences, Unicode strings, walkers)
body:
## Summary

`Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences` has no counterpart in `doublets`. A Rust consumer that needs sequences — and therefore strings — has to port the converter/walker stack by hand, while the C# consumer takes a `PackageReference` and is done.

## What is missing

Everything under `Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences` 0.6.5 that a store-backed string needs:

| C# type | Namespace |
|---|---|
| `BalancedVariantConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Converters` |
| `AddressToRawNumberConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Converters` |
| `RawNumberToAddressConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Converters` |
| `CachingConverterDecorator<TSource, TTarget>` | `Sequences.Converters` |
| `CharToUnicodeSymbolConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Unicode` |
| `UnicodeSymbolToCharConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Unicode` |
| `StringToUnicodeSequenceConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Unicode` |
| `UnicodeSequenceToStringConverter<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Unicode` |
| `RightSequenceWalker<TLinkAddress>` | `Sequences.Walkers` |
| `DefaultStack<TElement>` | `Platform.Collections.Stacks` |
| `TargetMatcher<TLinkAddress>` | `Data.Doublets` |

## Evidence

[link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli) ships the same CLI in C# and in Rust over the same store. The C# half references the package; the Rust half carries a hand-written port of every type above:

- [`rust/src/sequences/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/tree/3d53362125be47de595b0cad7a24fe4c3aeefd3d/rust/src/sequences) — 11 modules, ~360 lines, whose module doc reads *"Rust ports of the `Data.Doublets.Sequences` abstractions used by C#"*
- [`rust/src/unicode_string_storage.rs`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/3d53362125be47de595b0cad7a24fe4c3aeefd3d/rust/src/unicode_string_storage.rs) — ~440 lines assembling them into the C# `UnicodeStringStorage<uint>` pipeline

The C# side of the same feature is three `using` lines:

```csharp
using Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences.Converters;
using Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences.Walkers;
using Platform.Data.Doublets.Sequences.Unicode;
```

## Why upstream

Storing a string in a links database is not application logic — it is the same balanced-variant encoding for every consumer, and getting it wrong produces a database the C# tooling cannot read. Every Rust consumer that wants strings will otherwise re-derive the same encoding, and they will not agree with each other or with C#.

A `doublets::sequences` module (feature-gated, if the dependency weight is a concern) would let a consumer drop the port entirely.

Reported from link-foundation/link-cli#100, which asks that gaps found while updating to doublets 0.5.0 be filed here.

title: feat(decorators): port the C# decorator layer as zero-cost generic wrappers
body:
Closes #58.

Ports the decorator layer of `Platform.Data.Doublets` to Rust as generic wrappers that compose statically and fuse away at compile time.

## What is here

A new `doublets::decorators` module with all twelve C# decorators, each intercepting exactly the operations its C# counterpart does:

| C# decorator | This module | Create | Update | Delete | Each |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `LinksUniquenessValidator` | `UniquenessValidator` | | ● | | |
| `LinksUniquenessResolver` | `UniquenessResolver` | | ● | | |
| `LinksCascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver` | `CascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver` | | ● | ● | |
| `LinksUsagesValidator` | `UsagesValidator` | | ● | ● | |
| `LinksCascadeUsagesResolver` | `CascadeUsagesResolver` | | | ● | |
| `LinksInnerReferenceExistenceValidator` | `InnerReferenceExistenceValidator` | | ● | ● | ● |
| `LinksItselfConstantToSelfReferenceResolver` | `ItselfConstantToSelfReferenceResolver` | | ● | | ● |
| `LinksNullConstantToSelfReferenceResolver` | `NullConstantToSelfReferenceResolver` | ● | ● | | |
| `LinksNonExistentDependenciesCreator` | `NonExistentDependenciesCreator` | | ● | | |
| `NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver` | `NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver` | | | ● | |
| `LoggingDecorator` | `LoggingDecorator` | ● | ● | ● | |
| `NoExceptionsDecorator` | `NoExceptionsDecorator` | ● | ● | ● | ● |

Design, following the five constraints in the issue:

- **Static composition.** Every decorator is `D<T, L: Doublets<T>>` owning `L` by value. No `Box<dyn Links>`, no vtable.
- **`#[inline]` everywhere.** The `forward!` macro in `decorators/macros.rs` emits `#[inline]` on every pass-through method, so a layer that does not intercept an operation leaves no trace.
- **Policy as a type.** `Validate`, `Resolve` and `CascadeResolve` are zero-sized markers; `UniquenessPolicy` / `UsagesPolicy` map each to its decorator through a GAT, so `with_uniqueness(Resolve)` picks the layer at compile time.
- **No `dyn Error` in the hot path.** Everything stays in the crate's existing `Error<T>`.
- **A builder returning the concrete type.** `DecoratorsExt` takes the store by value:

```rust
use doublets::{decorators::{DecoratorsExt, Resolve}, mem, unit, Doublets};

let mut store = unit::Store::<usize, _>::new(mem::Global::new())?
    .with_uniqueness(Resolve)
    .with_usages_validation();
```

`with_automatic_uniqueness_and_usages_resolution()` builds the C# `AutomaticUniquenessAndUsagesResolution` stack in one call.

## The bug this fixes for callers (#57)

On a bare store, `create_link(a, b)` on an existing doublet inserts a duplicate and silently corrupts the index; deleting any of them then panics with `attempt to subtract with overflow` inside `platform-trees`. Reproduction kept at `experiments/issue-58/duplicate_corruption.rs`.

With `with_uniqueness(Resolve)`, `create_link` returns the existing link — exactly the `get_or_create` behaviour `link-assistant/router` open-codes today. `doublets/examples/uniqueness.rs` shows both sides:

```
bare store:
  create_link(1, 2) x8 -> [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]
  count = 10
  deleting any of them now panics in `platform-trees` (issue #57)

with_uniqueness(Resolve):
  create_link(1, 2) x8 -> [3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3]
  count = 3
  delete(3) -> ok, count = 2
  links = [1: 1 1, 2: 2 2]
```

`duplicate_creation_does_not_corrupt_the_index` in `doublets/tests/decorators.rs` is the automated version of that reproduction: it fails on a bare store and passes through the resolver.

## Fusion is checked, not assumed

`integration/tests/fusion.rs` builds `integration/src/bins/fusion-probe.rs` in release, disassembles it with `llvm-objdump`/`objdump`, and compares the emitted body of an operation on a **nine-layer** composed stack against the same operation on the bare store:

- `create` and `each`: the normalized instruction sequences are identical, and the composed `create` calls `unit::Store::create_links` directly — no decorator frame survives.
- `count`: the linker's identical code folding merged the two probes into one symbol, which is stronger still.

The test skips loudly (never fails spuriously) when no disassembler is present, the probe build fails, or the dump is unparsable, and honours `DOUBLETS_SKIP_FUSION_TEST`. It handles both GNU and LLVM objdump syntax and macOS `_`-prefixed symbols.

The probe build deliberately does not inherit the harness's compiler environment. `cargo llvm-cov` turns coverage on two different ways — through `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`, and since 0.9 through a `RUSTC_WRAPPER` that injects `-C instrument-coverage` for workspace crates (`src/wrapper.rs`). Coverage emits a counter per source region, so each *inlined* decorator layer still left a `lock incq` behind and the comparison failed in the coverage job while passing everywhere else — the bodies both called `Store::create_links` directly, so nothing had actually failed to fuse. The probe build now drops `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`, the rustdoc equivalents, `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` and every `*LLVM_COV*` variable, and skips outright if a coverage counter survives anyway rather than reporting a failure it did not observe.

Verified locally against cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.0, the version CI installs: `cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info` passes, the probe it builds carries 5 incidental `incq` from std instead of the 1908 an instrumented build emits, and the test compares all three operations rather than skipping.

`experiments/issue-58/verify-fusion.sh` is the negative control: it flips the `forward!` macro to `#[inline(never)]` and asserts the test then fails. It does, with the composed body calling `UniquenessValidator::create_links` where the bare one calls `Store::create_links` — so the check is not vacuous.

`decorators_add_no_state` additionally asserts via `static_assertions` that each decorator and the full automatic stack are the same size as the bare store.

## Also fixed: `unit::Store::update_links` reported the wrong `before`

Writing the decorator tests surfaced a pre-existing bug. `update_links` aliased the "old" values to the incoming change:

```rust
let old_source = source;   // the NEW source
let old_target = target;
```

so every write handler saw `before == after`. It now reads them off the link before the write, matching `split::Store`, which was already correct. Covered by `doublets/tests/write_handlers.rs` for both backends.

## Deviations from C#, all documented in `decorators/mod.rs`

- C# threads a `_facade` back-reference so a cascade re-enters at the top of the stack. A statically composed stack has no such back-reference; a decorator only knows the layers below it. For every stack C# itself builds the two coincide. Documented under "# Ordering".
- `UniquenessResolver` reports the *surviving* link to the handler, so `create_link` returns a valid address rather than the address of the link it just deleted.
- `CascadeUsagesResolver` tracks visited links, so a reference cycle terminates instead of overflowing the stack (covered by `cascade_usages_resolver_terminates_on_a_reference_cycle`).
- `MergeUsages` re-points sources and targets correctly; the C# version writes null targets because of a `params` constructor mix-up.
- `EnsureCreated` calls the creator in its loop; the C# loop never terminates.
- `InnerReferenceExistenceValidator::try_each_links` exists because `Links::each_links` has no error channel.
- `NoExceptionsDecorator` maps `Err(_)` to `Flow::Break`, the closest analogue of C#'s `Error` constant. It does not catch panics.
- `LoggingDecorator` surfaces the first writer I/O error instead of discarding it.

## Tests

- `doublets/tests/decorators.rs` — 20 tests, at least one per decorator, plus the #57 regression, the cycle case, the log-format check and the size assertions.
- `doublets/tests/write_handlers.rs` — 2 tests for the `before`/`after` fix on both backends.
- `integration/tests/fusion.rs` — the disassembly check.
- `doublets/examples/uniqueness.rs` — the before/after demonstration.

Full local CI parity is green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -Dwarnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo test --doc`, `cargo package -p doublets --list`, and the three `rust-script` checks.

Release is triggered by `changelog.d/20260829_120000_issue_58_decorators.md` (`bump: minor`); `Cargo.toml` is untouched, as the version-check job requires.

title: Port all C# decorators, composed as zero-cost abstractions that fuse into one function per operation
body:
`Platform.Data.Doublets` ships a decorator layer — 14 decorators over `LinksDecoratorBase`, composable in one call — and the Rust port has none of it. `src/` is `data`, `mem`, `lib.rs`: there is nothing to configure and nothing to wrap.

This asks for the **same decorators with the same logic**, ported faithfully from C#, but built so that a selected stack **compiles away entirely**: the user's chosen decorators should fuse into a single `create` / `update` / `delete` / `each` per store, with no indirection and no per-layer call at runtime.

## The decorators to port, and what each intercepts

| C# decorator | Create | Update | Delete | Each | Count |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `LinksUniquenessValidator` | | ● | | | |
| `LinksUniquenessResolver` | | ● | | | |
| `LinksCascadeUniquenessAndUsagesResolver` | | ● | ● | | |
| `LinksUsagesValidator` | | ● | ● | | |
| `LinksCascadeUsagesResolver` | | | ● | | |
| `LinksInnerReferenceExistenceValidator` | | ● | ● | ● | |
| `LinksItselfConstantToSelfReferenceResolver` | | ● | | ● | |
| `LinksNullConstantToSelfReferenceResolver` | ● | ● | | | |
| `LinksNonExistentDependenciesCreator` | | ● | | | |
| `NonNullContentsLinkDeletionResolver` | | | ● | | |
| `LoggingDecorator` | ● | ● | ● | | |
| `NoExceptionsDecorator` | ● | ● | ● | ● | ● |

Semantics should match C# so a store behaves identically in both languages; the *implementation* is free to be faster.

## Zero cost is achievable — measured, not assumed

Generic decorators (`D<L: Links>`, not `Box<dyn Links>`) monomorphise and inline away completely. Three stacked decorators over a store, versus the same logic written by hand as one function:

```rust
pub trait Links { fn create(&mut self, s: u64, t: u64) -> u64; }

pub struct Uniqueness<L: Links> { inner: L }   // if s == t { return 0 }
pub struct NullToSelf<L: Links> { inner: L }   // s = if s == 0 { 1 } else { s }
pub struct Usages<L: Links>     { inner: L }   // t = t + 1

#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn decorated_three(s: u64, t: u64) -> u64 {
    let mut l = Usages { inner: NullToSelf { inner: Uniqueness { inner: Store { n: 0 } } } };
    l.create(s, t)
}

#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn handwritten_fused(s: u64, t: u64) -> u64 { /* same logic, one function */ }
```

Release build, aarch64:

```
decorated_three   @ 0x0000000000000390
handwritten_fused @ 0x0000000000000390
```

**The same address.** The linker folded them because the three-decorator stack produced byte-identical machine code — five instructions, no calls:

```
390: add   x8, x1, #0x1
394: cmp   x0, #0x1
398: csinc x9, x0, xzr, hi
39c: eor   x0, x8, x9
3a0: ret
```

So "one function per operation, whatever the stack" is not aspirational — it is what the compiler already does, provided the design avoids the things that defeat it.

## Design constraints that keep it zero cost

1. **Static composition, not trait objects.** `Uniqueness<NullToSelf<Store>>` monomorphises; `Box<dyn Links>` forces a vtable call per layer and blocks fusion. C#'s `ILinks` field is the direct analogue of the latter — this is exactly where the Rust port should differ in implementation while keeping the logic.
2. **`#[inline]` on every forwarding method**, so cross-crate inlining works — a decorator in the library wrapping a store in user code must still fuse.
3. **Policy as a type, not a runtime flag.** A `Reject`/`Resolve`/`Allow` enum checked at runtime costs a branch per call; three zero-sized types selected at compile time cost nothing, and the unused arms vanish.
4. **No `dyn Error` in the hot path.** Boxing on the error path can pull allocation into the inlined body.
5. **A builder that returns the concrete composed type**, e.g. `Store::new(mem).with_uniqueness(Resolve).with_usages_validation()`, so the type is inferred and users never spell `Uniqueness<Usages<...>>` by hand while still getting a distinct monomorphised type.

A `#[cfg(test)]` check comparing the emitted symbol of a composed stack against a hand-fused equivalent — or simply asserting no `call` in the disassembly — would keep the property from regressing.

## Why this matters beyond ergonomics

Without any decorator layer, a Rust caller has no way to enable the uniqueness handling C# users can switch on in one call, and `create_link` on an existing `(source, target)` silently corrupts the index (#57 in this repo, with the details). Porting the decorators closes that gap; doing it zero cost means nobody has to weigh correctness against throughput to get it.

`link-assistant/router` is a concrete consumer: it works around the missing policy today by calling `get_or_create` everywhere, and would use a composed stack instead.

title: Fix CI/CD release pipeline for Cargo workspace repos

## Summary

Fixes #49

The CI/CD release pipeline failed at the "Auto Release" job because all release scripts assumed the root `Cargo.toml` contains a `[package]` section with `name` and `version` fields. In this workspace repository, the root `Cargo.toml` only has `[workspace]` — the package metadata lives in `doublets/Cargo.toml`.

**Error from failed run [#24406907038](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs/actions/runs/24406907038/job/71293199332):**
```
Detected single-language repository (Cargo.toml in root)
Error: Could not find name in ./Cargo.toml
```

## Root Causes

1. **Workspace Cargo.toml incompatibility** — All 9 release scripts read name/version from root `Cargo.toml` using regex, which fails on workspace-only manifests
2. **Pre-release version regex** — `bump-version.rs` used a regex that didn't match versions with pre-release suffixes like `0.1.0-pre+beta.15`
3. **Full-range PR diff in change detection** — `detect-code-changes.rs` compared the full PR range (`GITHUB_BASE_SHA..GITHUB_HEAD_SHA`), causing CI to run on every push even when the latest commit only touched non-code files (e.g. reverts of docs-only commits)

## Changes

- Added workspace-aware `Cargo.toml` resolution to all 9 release scripts:
  - Detects `[workspace]` in root manifest
  - Parses `members = [...]` list
  - Finds the first publishable member (skips `publish = false`)
  - Uses that member's `Cargo.toml` for name/version/publish operations
- Fixed `publish-crate.rs` to pass `-p <package>` flag for workspace repos
- Fixed `bump-version.rs` version regex to handle pre-release suffixes
- Aligned `detect-code-changes.rs` with the [rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template):
  - Switched from full PR range diffing to merge-commit-aware per-commit diffing (`HEAD^2^..HEAD^2`)
  - This ensures CI correctly skips jobs when only the latest push touches non-code files
  - Removed now-unused `GITHUB_BASE_SHA`/`GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` env vars from workflow
